newsitem.title: ITALY: FORECAST - Italy seen issuing 14.5 trln lire BOTs.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Italy seen issuing 14.5 trln lire BOTs.

text.p: Italy will continue to issue fewer short-term bills (BOTs) and favour longer-term debt instruments at the Treasury's mid-January BOT and zero coupon (CTZ) auction, which will see the debut of new 18-month CTZs, analysts said.

Analysts said their forecasts for this auction remained uncertain because they were still not sure of Treasury policy on the public sector borrowing requirement after 1996 PSBR, seen at a provisional 138.50 trillion lire, overshot the original 123.00 trillion lire target.

Analysts expect the Treasury to issue between 13.5 and 15.5 trillion lire BOT (for an average of 14.5 trillion lire) against 17.5 trillion lire maturing and 1.5 trillion to 2.0 trillion lire of the new 18-month CTZ.
"The new certificate must have a certain degree of liquidity in order to make it appealing," one analyst said.
The Treasury is seen likely to offer 2.0 trillion lire worth of a new tranche of two-year January 1, 1999 CTZs.
On Wednesday, the Treasury will detail the auction to be held on Friday. Settlement is on January 15.
